title: Provider credentials and OAuth tokens are persisted in renderer localStorage
reasoning: The frontend allow-list includes provider_api_keys and provider_oauth, and configStorage normalizes access_token, refresh_token, and api_key values into the object written directly to localStorage. In an Electron renderer, localStorage is accessible to any renderer compromise or injected script, so long-lived API keys and OAuth refresh tokens become much easier to exfiltrate than if they were held behind a main-process or OS credential boundary.
recommendation: Do not persist raw provider API keys or OAuth tokens in renderer localStorage. Store secrets in a main-process controlled credential store or OS keychain, expose only non-secret metadata such as connected/enabled/profile state to renderer config, and keep token access behind explicit IPC or SDK capability boundaries.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature, and a normal persistence round-trip test would likely assert the current insecure behavior unless it explicitly checks that secret fields are excluded from renderer storage.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a renderer config persistence test that saves provider_api_keys and provider_oauth with non-empty secret values, then asserts the serialized localStorage payload contains only safe metadata and no api_key, access_token, or refresh_token values.
minimumFixScope: Change the frontend config filter/storage contract to exclude raw secret fields from localStorage and add a secure credential-storage path for those values.
